messages.subject: fixnodes/fossil constraints in trait-dependent models
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I was just wondering if the possibility to constrain nodes to specific areas/trait states has been implemented in the trait-dependent version of BioGeoBEARS?

I've been trying to use fixnode and fixlikes as described for the general BioGeoBEARS models, but it's not working for me.

A little description of what I've done:
- I've tried a very simple case with a 1area geography and nullrange included. First, I ran the model with all parameters fixed except t12 and t21 (trait transition rates). This resulted in a relprobs matrix (res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node) with 4 columns. (I'm assuming here the following: column 1 = species present in null range + trait state 1; column 2: species present in region1 + trait state 1; column 3: species present in nullrange + trait state 2; column 4: species present in region 1 + trait state 2).
This resulted in the following probabilities for the root node:
c(0, 0.05, 0, 0.95).

- Then I tried constraining the root node as described for normal models, so I did
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$fixnode <- root_node
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$fixlikes <- c(0, 0.47, 0, 0.53)
I ran the model (no error messages), but the root node in the results had the following probabilities:
c(0, 0.04, 0, 0.96)

So things changed slightly in comparison to the original model, but it is far away from what I wanted to get as a result.

Can you help me?

Best,

Sarah

messages.body_plain:
Just a little side note: I tried fixing the root node in a simple DEC model, and the resulting probabilities of range occupancies did not match 100% the probabilities I had given to begin with (with BioGeoBEARS_run_object$fixnode). The difference is not gigantic (0.51 becomes 0.46; and 0.48 becomes 0.51 for the major ranges) but just enough to change the principal ancestral range. Is this normal behaviour or have I missed something?

Any help is greatly appreciated.

Best,

Sarah

messages.subject: Re: fixnodes/fossil constraints in trait-dependent models
messages.body_plain:
For all those in the future who might be struggling with the same issue as me: I think I misunderstood how exactly nodes are constrained in the models. It turns out that you can't suggest probabilities for range occupancies in the past, but you can just select a single range. So instead of giving probabilities to $fixlikes as I had done in my first try (BioGeoBEARS_run_object$fixlikes <- c(0, 0.47, 0, 0.53)) I just had to do: BioGeoBEARS_run_object$fixlikes <- c(0, 0, 0, 1) and everything worked!

messages.subject: Error in running DEC+j with areas allowed and time stratified matrix
messages.subject_clean: Error in running DEC+j with areas allowed and time stratified matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hi there everybody,

I've stumbled in a error while trying to run Dec+j with areas allowed and time stratified matrix.

Error in -details[[i, "hev"]]: invalid argument for unary operator

My code is this:
###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-
# DECTSTA+j ####
###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-###-
BioGeoBEARS_run_object = define_BioGeoBEARS_run()
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$trfn = trfn
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$geogfn = geogfn
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$max_range_size = max_range_size

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$min_branchlength = 0.000001    # Min to treat tip as a direct ancestor
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$include_null_range = TRUE    # set to FALSE for e.g. DEC* model, DEC*+J, etc.

#Time stritefied:
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$timesfn = timesfn2
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$dispersal_multipliers_fn = dispersal_multipliers_fn2
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$timesfn
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$dispersal_multipliers_fn
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$areas_allowed_fn = dispersal_areas_allowed_fn
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$areas_allowed_fn

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$speedup = TRUE
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$use_optimx = TRUE
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$num_cores_to_use = detectCores()
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$force_sparse = TRUE

BioGeoBEARS_run_object = readfiles_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)

# Divide the tree up by timeperiods/strata (uncomment this for stratified analysis)
BioGeoBEARS_run_object = section_the_tree(inputs=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table=TRUE, plot_pieces=FALSE, fossils_older_than = 0.5)
# The stratified tree is described in this table:
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$master_table

# Good default settings to get ancestral states
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$return_condlikes_table = TRUE
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$calc_TTL_loglike_from_condlikes_table = TRUE
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$calc_ancprobs = TRUE    # get ancestral states from optim run

# Look at the BioGeoBEARS_run_object; it's just a list of settings etc.
BioGeoBEARS_run_object
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$areas_allowed_fn
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$list_of_dispersal_multipliers_mats[[4]]

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table

# Set up DEC+J model
# Get the ML parameter values from the 2-parameter nested model
# (this will ensure that the 3-parameter model always does at least as good)
dstart = resDEC$outputs@params_table["d","est"]
estart = resDEC$outputs@params_table["e","est"]
jstart = 0.0001

# Input starting values for d, e
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","init"] = dstart
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","est"] = dstart
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["e","init"] = estart
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["e","est"] = estart

# Add j as a free parameter
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","type"] = "free"
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","init"] = jstart
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","est"] = jstart

# Run this to check inputs. Read the error messages if you get them!
check_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)

# For a slow analysis, run once, then set runslow=FALSE to just
# load the saved result.
runslow = TRUE
resfn = "DIP_DECTSTAj.Rdata"
if (runslow)
{
  res = bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
  res

  save(res, file=resfn)
  resDECTSTAj = res
} else {
  # Loads to "res"
  load(resfn)
  resDECTSTAj = res
}
What can this be?
Cheers.

Thank you & Cheers,
Torsten
